paras: New York's Attorney General asked a Manhattan court to order NovaTech's founders, <u>Cynthia and Eddy Petion</u>, to pay about <r>$1.37 billion</r>.
From 2019 to 2023, investors put in about <r>$1.16 billion</r> in crypto. NovaTech promised <r>2–4% a week</r>. It collapsed in 2023.
The couple fled the US. Four top promoters settled for nearly <g>$6 million</g>, which goes to victims.
slides.source: Decrypt, The Block, Cointelegraph · NY AG filing

paras: It spread through <u>prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole</u>, aimed at immigrant and religious communities.
It claimed to be a <r>registered, licensed broker</r>. It wasn't. Only about $26M ever reached a trading account.
<u>Weekly payouts came from new deposits.</u> 2–4% a week is over 140% a year: no real trading pays that.
